title: Understanding the 482 Salary Requirement: Hourly to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how the 482 salary requirement relates to hourly rates, casual loading, and super. Convert hourly to annual pay using 38 hours per week and 52 weeks.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: What is the 482 salary requirement and how does it relate to the minimum wage?
faqs.a: The 482 salary requirement is the minimum annual salary that must be paid to a Temporary Skill Shortage visa holder. It is based on the market salary rate for the occupation and is typically higher than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman ensures that 482 visa holders receive at least the same minimum entitlements under the National Employment Standards and any applicable award, including the minimum wage, casual loading, and superannuation.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks per year. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. If you are a casual employee, add 25% casual loading before the calculation. Remember that super is paid on top of this amount.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect the 482 salary requirement?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are employed as a casual on a 482 visa, your salary must include the 25% casual loading. The 482 salary requirement is based on the total remuneration, which can include casual loading. However, the base rate must still meet the market salary rate for the occupation. Always check your award or agreement for specific rules.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, understanding the full annual picture is essential. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For most full-time employees, the ordinary hours are 38 per week, as set by the National Employment Standards. This article explains how to calculate your annual gross pay, including casual loading and super, and how it relates to the **482 salary requirement**.

### The Basic Calculation

Assume a 38-hour week. If your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay is:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

This is before tax, super, and any other deductions. The same formula works for any hourly rate. For a part-time employee working fewer hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The fortnightly equivalent is weekly pay × 2, which helps when budgeting.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for award/agreement-free adult employees. Most employees are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries and roles. Award rates often include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. The **482 salary requirement** is typically above the award minimum because it must reflect the market salary rate for the occupation.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. The casual loading is paid on top of the minimum wage or award rate. For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When calculating annual pay for a casual, apply the loading to the hourly rate first, then multiply by hours and weeks. The **482 salary requirement** for a casual worker must include this loading.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer into a super fund. It is not deducted from your gross pay; it is paid on top. For the 2026–27 year, the super guarantee is 12%, with a maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual gross pay is $60,000, your employer must contribute $7,200 in super. This is separate from your salary and is a key part of your total remuneration package.

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold means you pay no tax on the first $18,200. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net income.

### The 482 Salary Requirement Explained

The **482 salary requirement** is the minimum annual salary that must be paid to a Temporary Skill Shortage (subclass 482) visa holder. It is not a fixed dollar amount; it is based on the market salary rate for the occupation. The Fair Work Ombudsman enforces that 482 visa holders receive the same minimum workplace rights as Australian employees, including the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super. The salary must be at least the Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT), which is updated periodically. However, the market rate may be higher. Always check the latest TSMIT figure from the Department of Home Affairs.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time employee on the minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80. This helps when comparing salary offers or planning expenses. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page can assist with quick calculations.

### Important Notes

This article provides estimates. Annual pay assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details on minimum wages, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. For information on casual loading, visit [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).
